attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The wording is firm ('are going to try'), so this is a forecast. 'The same' points back to Musk trying to 'control your mind' through an LLM he shapes. The normalised wording is fair, though it is mostly rhetorical framing ('you aren't paying attention').

contract.note: The contract rightly says an attempt at 'mind control' has no observable test and no contradiction condition. Changes to bias settings can be read as steering or as seeking neutrality. Treating it as not adjudicable is fair.

evidence.note: Meta hired an adviser on AI political bias in Aug 2025. This can be read as seeking neutrality or as steering. It covers Zuckerberg only; nothing in the packet covers Altman.

reviews.rationale: A firm but open-ended claim about intent to 'control minds', with no measure and no deadline. Nothing observable could show it false, and the one evidence item is ambiguous and covers only Meta. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The first part is hedged ('maybe a little closer to the center'), and the proposition keeps that with 'perhaps'. The second part is firm: Grok is hardly as far right as Musk. Only the firm part can be scored.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'not as far right as Musk' is ordinary and fair. The contract also folds the hedged 'maybe closer to center' into its support condition. Under policy that part is not scored, but the evidence is consistent with it anyway.

evidence.note: Independent test from Apr 2025: Grok-3 sat nearer the center than peers, while models overall stayed left of center. Consistent with both parts.
Jun 17, 2025: Grok said right-wing violence was deadlier, and Musk called that false. This shows Grok's outputs were less right-wing than Musk's views.
Grok 4 test from Jul 2025, after the target period. A similar pattern, but context only.

reviews.rationale: The firm part holds: in the period, Grok produced outputs Musk publicly rejected as not matching his views, and tests put it left of or near center. The hedged 'maybe closer to center' is not scored, though the Rozado test is consistent with it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'He is going to rewrite history/the data' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The failed alignment is a premise, rightly recorded as a qualifier. Reading 'history' as Grok's training corpus matches the post's 'rewrite the data'.

contract.note: The plain reading (a rewritten corpus used to retrain Grok) matches Musk's announced plan, which Marcus was responding to. Requiring Grokipedia to be shown as training data is a fair, ordinary line. The open horizon is correct.

evidence.note: Shows the premise held: Musk objected that Grok's output did not match his views. It is not evidence of whether the forecast came true.
Records Musk's June 2025 announcement of the plan. An announcement is not proof the plan was carried out.
As of Nov 2025, training Grok on Grokipedia was discussed only as a possibility, not documented.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The packet has no documentation that a released Grok model was trained on a rewritten corpus, and no record that xAI abandoned the plan. Neither early-resolution trigger is met by the evaluation date, so it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A general claim about how hard something is, with the same-data scope and the fine-tuning carve-out kept. The accuracy-cost part is hedged ('likely').

contract.note: The contract rightly notes there is no measure of 'standing out' and no threshold for 'pretty hard', and that fine-tuning, the main steering method, is carved out. The accuracy part is hedged. Not adjudicable is fair.

evidence.note: A 2024 preprint shows modest fine-tuning can steer a model's political lean. Fine-tuning is the case the claim carves out, and the study gives no accuracy-cost result.

reviews.rationale: 'Pretty hard' and 'stands out from the pack' have no measure. The main steering method is exempted, and the accuracy-cost part is hedged. No result could clearly confirm or refute it, so it is not adjudicable.
